premise.claim: Docs-only PR: 'Add a security model in English and Chinese that explains who may create, configure, and consume Fluid resources.' No linked issue, no runtime behavior change.
premise.evidence: Docs-only PR: premise validation is skipped per the review-pipeline carve-out. The documentation gap is real (security/ contained only self-assessment.md and images before this PR; no resource-tier/RBAC security model doc existed), and the files touched (security/) match the repo's established location for security docs.

integration.note: helm template only; no cluster needed. This is the L2 layer for a docs PR: the doc's control-plane RBAC claims are checked against the rendered chart, not just the templates.

findings.claim: The doc's cited code paths and symbols resolve in the repo (checks D2/D3). The 'local:// mountPoint becomes a hostPath on Jindo' claim (security/security-model.md Tier-1 Dataset row) is engine-specific: implemented by pkg/ddc/jindofsx and pkg/ddc/jindocache (the default JindoRuntime engine is jindocache), not by the legacy pkg/ddc/jindo engine.
Relative links inside the two new docs resolve; however no existing repo entry point (README.md, SECURITY.md, security/self-assessment.md 'Security links' table) links TO the new security model docs.

Doc claim 'csi.useNodeAuthorization: true (default) ... uses kubelet credentials for Node reads and patches' is accurate; the doc does not mention the silent fallback when the kubelet config file is missing (pkg/csi/plugins/register.go).

All other factual claims verified: CRD inventory (14+1), chart RBAC wildcards/helmDriver/failurePolicy (L1+L2), unprivileged sidecar mutator behavior, reference-Dataset access modes, EN/ZH YAML identity, label constants.

liveNote: No L3 live layer needed: the PR is documentation-only and does not change runtime behavior. The L2 helm-render layer covers the chart-claim verification the PR's own test plan describes.
